newsitem.title: CHILE: Chuquicamata strike unlikely - union boss.
newsitem.headline: Chuquicamata strike unlikely - union boss.

text.p: Supervisors at Codelco's Chuquicamata pit began voting Tuesday on whether to accept the state-owned company's final wage offer, but their union leader said he thought the workers would probably vote against a strike.
"I'd say it is about 30 percent against and 70 percent in favor (of accepting the company offer)," union leader Grimaldo Ponce told Reuters by telephone.
He said that the company had offered a four-year contract including a 3.5 percent real wage rise, plus a further nine percent rise conditional on reaching production targets.
Supervisors were largely happy with the money offered by Codelco, but many have expressed concern over their health care plans, which the company plans to switch to private control, Ponce said.
Union leaders discussed the company offer with their members at a meeting Monday evening, but the union has made no official recommendation on whether to accept the offer or not.
The 700-odd supervisors will vote on the offer in a ballot starting at 1000 local/1400 GMT and going on until 1800. The result should be known an hour or so after the urns close.

If the supervisors vote to reject the offer, Chilean law requires five days pass in which both sides can try to find a solution to the disagreement before a strike can legally begin at the first shift Saturday morning.
An initial vote to strike to pressure management in talks during the mandatory five day cooling-off period is a tactic commonly used by Chilean unions to extract concessions.
Chuquicamata's 7,000 miners went on strike for 10 days last year after scheduled wage talks broke down.
The mine, the largest of Codelco's four mining divisions, produced 632,000 tonnes of fine copper in 1996.
